# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** She made-prosper their works in the hand of a holy prophet.

**11:2** They went-through a trackless wilderness and pitched camp in impassable regions.

**11:3** They took-a-stand against enemies and repelled opponents.

**11:4** Being-thirsty they called-upon you, and water was-given to them from a sheer rock, and a cure for thirst from hard stone.

**11:5** For by what things their enemies were-punished, by these [things] they in-their-need were-benefited.

**11:6** Instead of a river's ever-flowing spring, fouled with blood as a rebuke to [the] decree of infanticide,

**11:7** you gave to-them abundant water unexpectedly,

**11:8** showing through the thirst that-had-been-brought-about at-that-time how you-had-punished their opponents.

**11:9** For when they were-tried, even though being-disciplined in mercy, they understood how the ungodly were being-tormented, being judged in wrath.

**11:10** For these ones you tested as a father warning; but those ones you examined as a stern king condemning.

**11:11** And whether absent or present, they were equally oppressed:

**11:12** for a double grief held them and a groaning at the memory of what-had-passed.

**11:13** For when they heard that through their own punishments the others had been benefited, they perceived the Lord.

**11:14** For whom they, having-cast-out long-ago, mockingly exposed — at the end of the outcome they marveled at him, thirsting differently than [did] the righteous.

**11:15** In return for the irrational thoughts of their unrighteousness, because of which, being-led-astray, they were-worshipping irrational serpents and worthless small-animals, you sent upon them a multitude of irrational animals for punishment,

**11:16** so that they might know that by what things one sins, by these [things] one is punished.

**11:17** For your all-powerful hand, that created the world from formless matter, was-not lacking the capacity to send upon them a multitude of bears or bold lions,

**11:18** or newly-created beasts unknown, filled with fury, either breathing out a blast of fire, or belching-forth a roar of smoke, or flashing terrible sparks from their eyes,

**11:19** which not only the harm of them could destroy them, but also the fearsome appearance [could] kill them.

**11:20** And even apart from these, they could-fall by a single breath, being-pursued by justice, and scattered by the breath of your power; but all things you ordered by measure and number and weight.

**11:21** For to-be-greatly-strong is always possible for you; and who will withstand the might of your arm?

**11:22** Because the whole world before you is as a turn-of-a-scale on a balance, and as a drop of morning-dew that-has-fallen upon the earth.

**11:23** But you have mercy on all, because you are-able to-do all-things, and you overlook the sins of men unto repentance.

**11:24** For you love all the-things-that-exist, and you loathe none of the-things you made; for you would-not have formed anything if you-hated [it].

**11:25** And how would anything have endured unless you willed it? Or how would-anything-have-been-preserved not called by you?

**11:26** But you spare all, because they are yours, O Master, lover-of-souls.
